subject: Volume pricing question: embeddings vs chat delta & commit tiers
messages:
From: Sophie Tran <sophie.tran@lumenix.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify rate card for high-volume use, embeddings vs chat

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the intro last week. We are pulling together numbers for our Q3 budget and need a clearer view of how Redwood's hosted API pricing would apply to Lumenix. High-level asks: 
- Example per-token rates for a 12–18 month commit at ~2B tokens/month (mixed embeddings + chat workload)
- How you treat model-specific deltas (standard vs premium models) and whether that delta is additive or multiplicative to the base rate
- Options for charging embeddings (per-token vs per-vector) and any minimums or slab bands
- Overage handling and whether blended rates are possible for mixed model usage

I've attached our RFP excerpt (Lumenix-RFP.pdf) with expected usage profile. Can you send a short proposal and any example math we can show finance?

Thanks,
Sophie
Sophie Tran
Head of ML Platforms, Lumenix
procurement cc: procurement@lumenix.com

Attachment: Lumenix-RFP.pdf (pdf)

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 12:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify rate card for high-volume use, embeddings vs chat

Hi Sophie — great to hear from you and thanks for the RFP. Quick summary up front, then I'll attach a short spreadsheet with worked examples.

TL;DR (high level):
- Base hosted per-token rate (standard chat): $0.0006 per token at 2B token/month commit (18 month).
- Premium chat models: 2.4x multiplier on base rate for latency-optimized/large context variants (applies per-token).
- Embeddings: we can do per-token at the same base with a 0.35x multiplier for dense embedding models, OR per-vector pricing when vectors are >64 dims and usage is stable (example: $0.00008 per vector).
- Blended rate: we offer a blended banding option if >70% of usage is one model family; otherwise billed per-model with monthly invoice-level usage aggregation and auto-blend option for overage calculation.
- Overage: tiered overage slabs (next 50% at -10% off list, beyond that at list).

I've attached a proposed worksheet (Lumenix-proposal-v1.xlsx) with three scenarios (chat-heavy, embed-heavy, mixed). Can we set a 30-min call Monday to walk through a worked example with finance?

Best,
Neha Kapoor

Hi Sophie — jumping in with the worked numbers you asked for (short). Below are two simple invoice-level examples using the 60/25/15 mix you provided and Neha's base list rate.

Example A — model-level billing (no blending):
- Base chat tokens (60% of 2,000,000,000 = 1.2B tokens) @ $0.0006 = $720,000
- Premium chat tokens (25% = 500M) @ $0.0006 * 2.4 = $0.00144 => $720,000
- Embedding tokens (15% = 300M) @ $0.0006 * 0.35 = $0.00021 => $63,000
- Subtotal (list) = $1,503,000
- Commit discount (example 20% off list for 18-month 2B commit) => $1,202,400
- Net effective blended rate = $1,202,400 / 2B = $0.0006012 per token

Example B — invoice-level blended approach (apply single blended factor before model delta):
- Start with commit discounted base: $0.0006 * (1 - 0.20) = $0.00048
- Apply model multipliers on discounted base: 
  - Standard chat: $0.00048
  - Premium chat: $0.00048 * 2.4 = $0.001152
  - Embeddings: $0.00048 * 0.35 = $0.000168
- Invoice total equals same arithmetic as A in this particular mix; difference emerges when overages are priced using list vs discounted base.

Notes:
- Our standard is to apply the commit discount to the base rate first, then apply model multipliers (so premium remains proportional to the discounted base). That makes finance reporting cleaner.
- Per-vector billing is available but requires a minimum monthly commitment for vectors and is metered separately; if you expect stable embedding throughput we can shift to per-vector and cap token invoicing.
- Overage blending: if overage remains within the same model mix band for the month, we can auto-apply the same commit discount to overage up to the first slab. Beyond that, overage falls back to list slabs.

I'll put a short formal quote together with those assumptions (and opt-in for per-vector example).

—Marissa
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
